Course Overview

The course is organized into sections. Each one opens with a lecture and continues with hands-on activities, and each section builds on the one before it.

6 sections · 3 lectures · 3 hands-on activities

1

Foundations of Microbial Population Genomics

Microbial evolution, mutation, recombination, population structure, genetic diversity, and species delineation.

    2

    Taxonomic Classification and Genomic Subtyping

    Genome-based species identification, MLST, k-mer-based methods, and other microbial typing approaches.

    1. Lecture What Is a Species?
    2. Lecture Genome-Based Species Identification
    3. Activity When Names and Genomes Disagree: E. coli and Shigella
    4. Lecture Subtyping Below the Species Level
    5. Activity Cataloged Names vs. Agnostic Clusters: MLST and Floc
    6. Activity Optional: One Species, Many Subtypes: Influenza A
    3

    High-Resolution Genomic Relatedness

    Core genome MLST (cgMLST), core-SNP analysis, genomic distance, clustering, and analytical limitations.

      4

      Phylogenetic Methods and Tree Building

      Evolutionary models, tree-building methods, rooting, branch lengths, support values, and tree interpretation.

        5

        Interpreting Phylogenomic Evidence in Outbreak Investigations

        Genomic clusters, background diversity, epidemiological integration, uncertainty, and transmission inference limitations.

          6

          Integrated Genomic Epidemiology Case Studies

          Applying typing, genomic relatedness, phylogenetics, and epidemiological evidence to outbreak investigation scenarios.
